answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake that grows with the value of jobs it takes, like a willow that bends but stays rooted. A new identity starts at dawn with only tiny, low-value tasks, so an attacker must fund thousands of stakes to flood the ocean of listings, and any proven fraud slashes the stake and burns the agent's earned reputation. Creating fake identities then costs real money while honest agents keep their bond and history.
